literature_notes: The ledger contains two clips (L1, L2) about a FLAG-tagged COL13A1 construct expressed in MCF-10A cells. L1 describes cloning the full-length protein into a 'FLAG-tagged pCDH-EF1-MCS-T2A-Puro' lentiviral vector. This is a commercial vector whose FLAG tag position relative to the insert is not stated anywhere in the ledger clips — the clips name neither the terminus nor a residue at which the FLAG is placed. The rules explicitly disqualify 'a commercial plasmid whose tag POSITION is unstated; you cannot pin insert_after_residue.' Even attempting a topology_derived inference is blocked: COL13A1 is a type II transmembrane protein with its N-terminus intracellular (residues 1–46) and its C-terminus extracellular (residues 62–717), so there is exactly one extracellular terminus — but the ledger does not tell us whether the FLAG is on the N-terminal (intracellular) or C-terminal (extracellular) end of the protein. The forward primer in L1 (5′-AATTGCTAGCGCCACCATGGTAGCGGAGCGCACCCAC-3′) begins at M1 of COL13A1, which is consistent with either orientation. L2 confirms expression by western blot in cell lysates only — no surface-detection assay (flow cytometry, non-permeabilized immunofluorescence, surface biotinylation) is reported, so even if the position were known the validation level would be at most detected_only. Because the tag position is genuinely indeterminate from the ledger, no site can be proposed, and zero is the correct answer.
